title: Shifting Left: Accessibility in CI/CD 🚀
description: Integrate accessibility checks into your development pipeline and culture to catch issues early.

slides.title: Shift Left: Catch Bugs Before Production 🐛
slides.content:
"Shift left" means moving testing earlier in the development lifecycle.

- Instead of an audit right before launch, integrate tests during coding.
- Tools can run on every pull request, blocking merges if new accessibility issues are found.

This reduces the cost and effort of fixing accessibility problems – a bug found in design is 10x cheaper than in production.

quizData.question: What does 'shift left' mean in accessibility?

options.text: Moving all testing to the user
Testing earlier in the development cycle

quizData.explanation: Testing early and often, integrated into the developer workflow.

slides.title: Tools for CI/CD Integration ⚙️
slides.content:
Add accessibility checks to your pipeline:

- **axe‑core** + Playwright/Cypress: write automated tests that assert no accessibility violations on key pages.
- **Lighthouse CI**: set a minimum accessibility score (e.g., 90); fail the build if it drops.
- **pa11y‑ci**: run pa11y on deployed environments, generate reports.
- **GitHub Actions** / **GitLab CI**: run these on every PR.

Start with a low‑bar baseline (e.g., no critical/serious issues) and tighten over time.

slides.title: axe‑core with Playwright Example

quizData.question: What is the main advantage of failing a build when axe finds a new accessibility violation?

options.text: It prevents new accessibility bugs from reaching production

quizData.explanation: Blocking merges on violations ensures the codebase doesn't regress.

slides.title: Testing in Design & Storybook 🎨
slides.content:
Even before code, accessibility can be tested:

- **Figma plugins**: Stark, Contrast, Focus Order.
- **Storybook a11y addon**: runs axe on each component story in isolation.
- **Linting**: eslint‑plugin‑jsx‑a11y warns about missing alt, label‑for, etc.

Shift left to the design phase – accessible design reduces rework.

slides.title: Building an Accessibility Culture 🧑‍🤝‍🧑
slides.content:
Tools alone aren't enough. Foster a culture:

- Train the whole team on accessibility basics.
- Include accessibility in the definition of done.
- Celebrate accessibility wins.
- Appoint an accessibility champion.

Accessibility is everyone's responsibility, not just a specialist's.

quizData.question: Who is responsible for accessibility in a team?

options.text: Everyone: designers, developers, testers, product owners

quizData.explanation: Accessibility must be a shared team responsibility to be effective.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Start small
Add one automated check to your CI today. Then add another next sprint. Progress over perfection.
